subject.title: [Bug]: `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` breaks `openai-codex` auth/keychain paths on macOS and can fail fresh runtime launch with `SecItemCopyMatching failed -50`

question: Should OpenClaw preserve the macOS launchd `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` default and add a scoped Codex/keychain auth boundary, or change the service TLS default itself?
rationale: Both choices affect upgrade-sensitive auth and launch behavior: the default protects service TLS, while the reported failure shows it may poison keychain-backed Codex auth in fresh runtime paths.

options.title: Scope the auth/keychain boundary
options.body: Keep the macOS service TLS default, prevent keychain/status/fresh launch auth reads from inheriting the problematic CA mode, and require live macOS proof.

options.title: Change the macOS service default
options.body: Remove or narrow the global system-CA default, accepting the risk of re-opening launchd TLS failures unless separate TLS proof covers them.

options.title: Treat as legacy-provider migration only
options.body: Close the `openai-codex` surface in favor of doctor migration to canonical `openai`, but only if maintainers decide fresh Codex keychain launch failures are outside current support.

recommendation.title: Scope the auth/keychain boundary
recommendation.body: Keep the macOS service TLS default, prevent keychain/status/fresh launch auth reads from inheriting the problematic CA mode, and require live macOS proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest combined history across Codex keychain reads, Node startup TLS planning, and external CLI auth scoping.
